Its parameter-source link points to OpenRouter’s general Baidu list. This is not an independently supported specification or a developer statement identifying a base model.

release_date.note: Earliest documented public availability in the accessed evidence: OpenRouter explicitly labels this exact model released May6,2026. Retain the provider-documented release date with this provenance; the original developer announcement date remains unresolved and the later May9/June9 reports are not substituted for it.

open_weights.note: Closed under the user-requested availability rule: Baidu documents Cobuddy integration and hosted access, but no public downloadable Cobuddy checkpoint was located in its official inventory or exact-name weight search. Enterprise local deployment and other open ERNIE/Qianfan models do not establish public Cobuddy weights. This is current availability, not a proprietary-ownership determination.

license.note: No exact-model license or supported proprietary distribution classification was verified. Service availability is insufficient to infer a weight license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 English/Chinese exact-name searches and original/later developer-source checks found no nominal total count or explicit relationship to a publicly sized base. The concrete 21B lead is expressly a third-party estimate from positioning and neighboring lightweight ERNIE models. Baidu’s Lightmate article identifies Cobuddy as an integrated model, not as a sized Comate/ERNIE derivative. Null reflects absent nominal evidence, not a requirement for exact deployed tensors.

active_parameters_b.note: Rechecked independently on October 27. No Cobuddy activated count or activation convention appears in exact-model documentation, the developer post, the later ERNIE 5.1 comparison or current provider tables. The 3B lead is paired with an explicitly speculative 21B estimate and has no named-base support. No architecture, total-equals-active assumption or ERNIE sibling activation count is inherited.

architecture.note: No accessed exact-model source identifies dense/MoE structure or Transformer configuration. ERNIE technical disclosures and third-party architecture estimates do not establish Cobuddy architecture.

context_window.note: Novita explicitly reports 131,072 tokens for baidu/cobuddy; its model page rounds this to 128K. This is the documented served context limit.

patch.notes: Baidu identifies Cobuddy as a code-generation model; Novita documents its served capabilities. Nominal total and active counts remain undisclosed; the 21B/3B estimate has no developer-confirmed base lineage. Architecture, license and family remain unresolved. May 6, 2026 is the earliest provider-documented public release, corroborated by Baidu confirming availability on May 9; the original developer announcement date remains unresolved. Classified closed because no public downloadable Cobuddy checkpoint was found.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains null/undisclosed total and active counts after fresh developer and provider checks, Chinese/English nominal-size and lineage searches, and later comparison review. Resolved the concrete 21B/3B lead to an explicitly speculative estimate based on related ERNIE models, with no developer mapping. Reverified the Comate article byline and original developer post. All other field assessments are preserved. October 28 availability review: Classified closed because no public downloadable Cobuddy checkpoint was found. All thirteen unrelated field assessments and prior research metadata are preserved.

availability_resolution.classification_rule: Open means an identified public downloadable checkpoint for this exact model or a developer-documented equivalent; otherwise closed under the user-requested practical availability rule. This is not a legal ownership or perpetual-closure finding.
